Primary references for the algorithms in pladdrr

Source: R/pladdrr-references.R
pladdrr-references.Rd

pladdrr does not implement new methods: it compiles Praat's own C/C++ routines and returns what the Praat application returns. The methods below are the published sources those routines are based on, grouped by what you call in pladdrr. Praat's own documentation (https://www.fon.hum.uva.nl/praat/manual/) describes the exact variant each command uses, and states where Praat departs from the paper. Where a pladdrr result is checked against the Praat application, the check is in tests/testthat/test-praat-faithfulness.R.

Software

  • Boersma, P. & Weenink, D. Praat: doing phonetics by computer. https://praat.org/. Cite the Praat version bundled with the package (see citation("pladdrr")).

Pitch (to_pitch_ac, to_pitch_cc, to_pitch_shs) and harmonicity (to_harmonicity_ac, to_harmonicity_cc)

  • Boersma, P. (1993). Accurate short-term analysis of the fundamental frequency and the harmonics-to-noise ratio of a sampled sound. Proceedings of the Institute of Phonetic Sciences, University of Amsterdam, 17, 97-110. (autocorrelation and cross-correlation pitch, harmonics-to-noise ratio)

  • Hermes, D. J. (1988). Measurement of pitch by subharmonic summation. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, 83(1), 257-264. doi:10.1121/1.396427 (to_pitch_shs)

Formants (to_formant_burg, to_lpc_burg)

  • Burg, J. P. (1975). Maximum entropy spectral analysis. PhD thesis, Stanford University. (Burg's linear-prediction algorithm)

Cepstral peak prominence and voice-quality indices (get_cpps, calculate_cpps_ultra, get_cpps_fast)

  • Hillenbrand, J., Cleveland, R. A. & Erickson, R. L. (1994). Acoustic correlates of breathy vocal quality. Journal of Speech and Hearing Research, 37(4), 769-778. doi:10.1044/jshr.3704.769

  • Hillenbrand, J. & Houde, R. A. (1996). Acoustic correlates of breathy vocal quality: dysphonic voices and continuous speech. Journal of Speech and Hearing Research, 39(2), 311-321. doi:10.1044/jshr.3902.311

  • Maryn, Y., Corthals, P., Van Cauwenberge, P., Roy, N. & De Bodt, M. (2010). Toward improved ecological validity in the acoustic measurement of overall voice quality: combining continuous speech and sustained vowels. Journal of Voice, 24(5), 540-555. doi:10.1016/j.jvoice.2008.12.014 (AVQI)

  • Maryn, Y. & Weenink, D. (2015). Objective dysphonia measures in the program Praat: smoothed cepstral peak prominence and acoustic voice quality index. Journal of Voice, 29(1), 35-43. doi:10.1016/j.jvoice.2014.06.015 (the Praat implementation of both)

  • Siegel, A. F. (1982). Robust regression using repeated medians. Biometrika, 69(1), 242-244. doi:10.1093/biomet/69.1.242 (the default robust trend fit for CPPS)

Cepstral coefficients (to_mfcc)

  • Davis, S. B. & Mermelstein, P. (1980). Comparison of parametric representations for monosyllabic word recognition in continuously spoken sentences. IEEE Transactions on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing, 28(4), 357-366. doi:10.1109/TASSP.1980.1163420

Speech synthesis (KlattGrid)

  • Klatt, D. H. (1980). Software for a cascade/parallel formant synthesizer. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, 67(3), 971-995. doi:10.1121/1.383940

  • Klatt, D. H. & Klatt, L. C. (1990). Analysis, synthesis, and perception of voice quality variations among female and male talkers. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America, 87(2), 820-857. doi:10.1121/1.398894

Dynamic time warping (DTW)

  • Sakoe, H. & Chiba, S. (1978). Dynamic programming algorithm optimization for spoken word recognition. IEEE Transactions on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing, 26(1), 43-49. doi:10.1109/TASSP.1978.1163055

Other modules

Jitter, shimmer, intensity, LTAS, spectrograms, PCA, discriminant analysis, the Cochleagram and Excitation auditory models and the remaining classes follow the definitions in Praat's manual rather than a single primary paper; vignette("terminology") states the definition each result uses.

Value

No return value; this page only documents the references.
